rubric.why: Identifies hacking as access without authorization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hacking involves accessing a computer or system without permission.

rubric.why: Identifies the target of the unauthorized access.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a computer, system, network, or its data as the target.

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorized access to a computer, computer system, or network.
It may be done to view, steal, change, or damage data.

rubric.why: States that hardware resources are shared among computers or users.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that hardware sharing makes hardware resources available to more than one computer or user.
Award 1 mark for a correct example such as a printer, disk, or scanner.

modelAnswer: Hardware sharing means allowing multiple computers or users to use the same hardware resources.
For example, computers on a network can share a printer.

items.followUp: What is meant by receiver in data communication?

rubric.why: Identifies the sender as the source of the communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the sender is the source or originating device/person.
Award 1 mark for explaining that the sender transmits data, information, or a message to a receiver.

modelAnswer: A sender is the person or device that is the source of a communication.
It sends or transmits data or a message to the receiver.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a router in a network?

rubric.why: Identifies that routing involves choosing a path or route.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that routing determines or selects a path for data.

rubric.why: Explains that data is directed toward its destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that routing forwards or directs data/packets from a source toward a destination.

modelAnswer: Routing is the process of selecting a path for data to travel through a network.
It directs or forwards data packets from the source to the destination.

items.followUp: What is the function of FTP?

rubric.why: Identifies the information or content HTTP transfers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HTTP is used to transfer hypertext or web pages.

rubric.why: Identifies the communication between a web server and a client/browser.
rubric.description: Communication between web client and server
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HTTP enables communication or data transfer between a browser/client and a web server.

modelAnswer: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer hypertext and web pages on the World Wide Web.
It enables a web browser or client to communicate with a web server.

items.followUp: What is an HTML anchor used for?

rubric.why: Explains the function of a hyperlink.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a hyperlink connects to another web page or resource.

rubric.why: Distinguishes an anchor as a location or target, commonly within a page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that an anchor marks or links to a particular location, often within the same page.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink is a clickable link that takes the user to another web page or resource.
An anchor identifies a particular location in a page, so a link can jump directly to that location.

items.followUp: Draw a flowchart showing how to determine whether a number is even or odd.

rubric.why: Gives the use of the terminal symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an oval/terminal symbol represents the start or end of a flowchart.

rubric.why: Gives the use of the process symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a rectangle represents processing, an instruction, or a calculation.

rubric.why: Gives the use of the input/output symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a parallelogram represents input or output of data.

rubric.why: Gives the use of a decision, flow-line, or connector symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining that a diamond represents a decision/condition, an arrow shows flow direction, or a connector joins separated parts of a flowchart.

modelAnswer: An oval (terminal) symbol shows the start or end of a flowchart.
A rectangle (process) symbol shows an instruction, operation, or calculation.
A parallelogram (input/output) symbol shows data being entered or displayed.
A diamond (decision) symbol shows a condition with alternative outcomes.
An arrow (flow line) shows the direction of the steps.
A small circle (connector) joins separated parts of a flowchart.
